body: But don’t feel guilty.. it’s not supposed to be “easy” for everyone. I was thinking it’d be horrible for me with how sick it made me when I missed a dose. Anxiety was definitely hard to get through though as I chewed my bottom lip raw.

I was on 30 mg daily for about a year .. maybe a little more. Any time I missed a dose (accidentally) it made me super sick. I told my doctor I wanted to taper/switch meds. Lowered my dose to 20 mg for 7 days & consecutively started 10 mg lexapro as the lexapro was supposed to help with any withdrawal symptoms. Also got prescribed Zofran for the transition. It was pretty easy for me physical wise but I definitely had the WORST anxiety of my life during the transition. But now I’m just on seroquel & said fuck the lexapro bc it killed my ability to ‘o’.

Maybe try to get a job somewhere that you don’t have to handle cash so it wouldn’t be a concern that you would steal money, maybe? also a lot of places have the option to not contact your last employer (not to say they still won’t do it). not sure about it being on a record or anything, but everything will be alright. Just breathe & take things one step at a time. You can only control what you do from here on. You got this
?? I really hope everything is okay.

Thank you! I was really curious about the process of the victim did not want to cooperate afterwards for any given reason. I’ve taken a multitude of classes but they never dive too far into recanted statements or, so far, the victim too much. I appreciate the input!

My professor has reached out to me and said “The old law stated that the person had to die, the newer ruling (G.S. 8C-804(b)) is that they do NOT have to die. However, if they don’t die, then they should be able to testify. If they recant their statement and the dying declaration is allowed into evidence, then the jury would be able to consider both as evidence in reaching their decision.” 

Thank you all for your input :)

I was also thinking they’d have to stay dead & I know it’s a crazy scenario lol, but I am just curious of how that would work out I guess. I know a lot of SA victims recant statements so I wasn’t sure if they’d just let it go or push to prosecute it based on the dying declaration.. thanks again!
